# Create an improved Phase Shift effect

## Problem statement

The current Phase Shift treatment — a static dark-blue desaturation overlay plus a
cyan/red chromatic split — is not distinctive enough: when the ship phases out the
player has to look for a subtle tint to confirm it, and enemies arriving out of the
wormhole carry no visual warning at all that they are "not fully here". The ask is a
"shimmer" and "glitch" read so a phased entity is unmistakably in a different state.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, when my ship phases out — or when enemies
  emerge from the wormhole at the start of a wave — I want them to shimmer and glitch
  so it is instantly obvious they are not in their usual state."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the auto Phase Shift, I want the
  effect to visibly 'fire' at the moment of activation so I can trust it and time my
  flying accordingly."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want the shimmer/glitch behaviour to
  live once in the shared core/VFX layer so the shipped game and every combat gym look
  identical and cannot diverge (gym↔game parity convention)."

Example user stories:

- *"My ship phased out mid-bullet-hell and I didn't even notice — I want the screen to
  ripple and shimmer the instant phase fires, then keep pulsing so I know the state is
  still on."*
- *"Scouts poured out of the wormhole and I couldn't tell they were materialising — I
  want each one to flicker and glow as it grows, so I read 'not solid yet'."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Player phase activation burst (glitch).** On the frame the Phase Shift activates (`isPhased` rising edge) the screen-wide treatment emits a brief **ripple/burst** — e.g. a short sharp chromatic-split surge with a flicker step — that reads as a "glitch" hit, distinct from the player-death juice (no camera shake; the existing screen-wide overlays are retained).
- **Continuous player shimmer while phased.** While `isPhased` stays true the treatment sustains a **continuous shimmer**: the existing cyan/red chromatic split becomes **more vivid and pulsing** — higher alpha (raised from 0.10 toward ~0.20), wider offset (raised from 3 px toward ~6 px) with a slow oscillation — plus a subtle alpha flicker (≈2–4 Hz) and a soft colour-pulse between the two split hues. All magnitudes exported as tunable constants with per-layer `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggles (mirroring the current `phaseShiftJuice` pattern). Phase expiry clears every layer on the falling edge, leaving no residual tint.
- **Per-enemy shimmer/glitch during wormhole emergence (no screen-space effects).** Each enemy growing from the wormhole gets a **per-entity** treatment over its growth window (`ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`): a brief ripple burst as it starts to materialise, then a continuous shimmer — a subtle scale/alpha flicker plus a soft colour-pulse on the entity itself — all driven from the shared spawn-animation path (`updateSpawnAnimation`) so `PlayScene` and every gym behave identically. No screen-wide overlay is introduced for the emergence path.
- **Wormhole-position glow/pulse ring.** While a wormhole is open for a wave the wormhole itself gets a subtle glow/pulse ring (radius pulse + soft glow at the wormhole position, drawn once per wormhole, tracked in the existing `wormholeEffects` registry and cleared when the wormhole closes). Visually distinct from both the phase-shift treatment and the player-death juice.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover: pure params model (new tunables mapped verbatim, toggles honoured), activation burst + continuous shimmer layer creation/teardown (edge-triggered, no residual layers), per-enemy shimmer driven by the spawn-state window, wormhole ring lifecycle, the no-camera-shake regression for Phase Shift, and safe-no-op behaviour headless. `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 (juice) is updated with the new shimmer/glitch treatment and tunables, and code comments document every new constant. The full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **No camera shake** (established producer decision — shake made Phase Shift read
  like player-death juice; the regression test asserting "never shakes" stays).
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): the shimmer/glitch behaviour lives once in the
  shared core/VFX layer (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`,
  the shared `CombatCoreScene`/`CombatScene` spawn path) and is consumed by both
  `PlayScene` and the gyms — no divergent copies (duplicate-body guard + gym-parity
  docs assertion apply).
- **Screen-wide effects only for the player phase path.** The enemy-emergence path is
  per-entity/per-wormhole only — the producer explicitly chose "no screen space
  effects" for spawning enemies.
- Keep the existing cyan/red split identity (producer Q3 = A: more vivid, not
  recoloured); keep per-layer toggles and the pure `resolve*Params()` pattern.
- Safe no-op without a Phaser render context (headless tests); no new runtime
  dependencies; performance-neutral (tweens/alpha only, no per-frame allocations
  beyond the existing pattern).

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — screen-wide Phase Shift treatment: dark-blue
  dim overlay (α 0.22) + cyan/red chromatic split (α 0.1, 3 px offset), edge-triggered
  `update(active, dt)` (the `dt` param is currently unused — reserved for pulsing).
  Camera-shake regression and pure-param tests in `phaseShiftJuice.test.ts`.
- `CombatCoreScene._updatePhaseShiftJuice(dt)` lazily constructs the controller and
  drives it from `getEffectsRegistry().isPhased` — shared by `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`.
- `applyPhaseGhost` (`CombatEffectVisuals.ts`) sets the ship ghost alpha while phased
  (unchanged; per-entity shimmer is additive and must not fight it).
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — wormhole open (1 s) → enemy growth
  (`ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` = 1.5 s via `startSpawnAnimation`/`updateSpawnAnimation`/
  `isEnemySpawning`) → close (0.5 s); `WormholeController` guarantees at most one live
  wormhole; `spawnWormholeOpen/Close` handles.
- `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` each drive spawn updates from `updateSpawnAnimation`
  and open/close the single wormhole from `this._wormhole` with the `wormholeEffects`
  registry (`CombatScene.wormholeEffects`, cleared on `SHUTDOWN`).

## Desired change

- In `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`: raise split alpha/offset and add a slow pulsing
  oscillation and an activation ripple/burst + continuous shimmer/flicker layer, all
  under tunables/toggles; keep edge-triggered apply/clear and the no-shake guarantee.
- In `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`: add per-entity shimmer/glitch helpers driven from the
  spawn-growth window (burst on growth start, then flicker/pulse while growing), and a
  wormhole glow/pulse ring tied to the wormhole's open lifetime.
- Wire the per-entity shimmer into the shared spawn path so `PlayScene` and the gyms
  consume it identically; wire the wormhole ring into the existing `wormholeEffects`
  registry lifecycle.
- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 and code comments; extend the unit tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — **Edit**: vivid/pulsing split, activation burst,
  continuous shimmer layers, new tunables/toggles.
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` — **Edit**: params, burst/shimmer, no-shake, edge
  trigger, teardown.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — **Edit**: per-enemy shimmer/glitch helpers +
  wormhole glow/pulse ring.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — **Edit**: new helper tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: any
  shared wiring needed to drive the new effects (e.g. pass spawn state, ring
  lifecycle) without divergent copies.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: consume the shared emergence-path
  helpers; no new behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — **Edit (minimal)**: consume the same
  shared helpers (parity).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: §7.2 juice description + new tunables.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Over-stimulation / seizure sensitivity* — shimmer, flicker and glitch bursts can be
  uncomfortable. Mitigation: keep magnitudes small and durations short, drive every
  layer from exported tunables with per-layer toggles (consistent with existing juice
  practice); player shimmer uses a gentle ≈2–4 Hz flicker, not rapid strobe; a
  reduce-motion accessibility option is out of scope here (separate tracked idea).
- *Player-death overlap* — the burst must not read as death juice. Mitigation: keep
  the no-camera-shake regression, reuse the chromatic-split identity only (never the
  death ring/flash palette), and keep the burst short (~150–250 ms).
- *Parity drift* — PlayScene/gym copies diverge. Mitigation: implement once in the
  shared core/VFX modules; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs
  assertion enforce this.
- *Per-frame cost* — pulsing/flicker must not allocate per frame. Mitigation: use
  Phaser tweens and existing object reuse; no new particle emitters beyond the ring.
- *Scope creep* — the "glitch" ask could balloon into post-processing shaders.
  Mitigation: keep to the current overlay/entity technique (no render-to-texture or
  shader work); record any shader-grade effect as a separate linked item.

**Assumptions** (producer-validated via Q1–Q3)

- *Player shimmer/glitch* = activation burst then continuous shimmer, **with** the
  existing screen-wide treatment retained and made more vivid/pulsing (producer: "for
  players D — with screen space effects"; Q3 = A).
- *Emerging enemies* = per-entity shimmer/glitch (burst + shimmer) **without** any
  screen-wide effect, plus a subtle wormhole-position glow/pulse ring (producer:
  "spawning enemies D — no screen space effects"; "B + wormhole effect — no screen
  space effects").
- The existing cyan/red split palette is retained (vivid, not recoloured).
- The ship's ghost alpha (`applyPhaseGhost`) is unchanged; per-entity shimmer is
  applied to emergent enemies only, not to the player's ship object itself.
- The effect is purely cosmetic: gameplay, hitboxes and spawn protection are
  unchanged.

## Related work

See the automated "Related work (automated report)" section below (added by the
`find-related` skill).

- Phase shift needs to be auto-applied when needed (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8) — *completed*;
  parent of the existing automatic Phase Shift and its juice module.
- Phase Shift juice module (AH-0MUJRGWGG0073JWS) — *completed*; the module this work
  upgrades (screen-wide dim + chromatic split, no shake).
- PlayScene: add P6 phase-shift ghost visual (AH-0MU8QVC9Y008R8I5) — *completed*; the
  ship ghost-alpha precedent (`applyPhaseGhost`).
- Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice) (AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) —
  *completed*; reference for a layered, toggleable juice module and the defeat glitch
  flicker pattern.
- P6 charge and permanent auto-trigger model (AH-0MUJRGVQE004XA1T) — *completed*;
  introduced the Phase Shift auto-trigger the juice must clearly communicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What specific visual effects should 'shimmer' and 'glitch' include?** Options:
  (A) rapid alpha flickering + colour cycling on the existing overlays; (B) screen-space
  distortion (pixel displacement / chromatic aberration wobble); (C) per-entity
  ripple/burst on activation + noise-like overlay flicker; (D) combination: brief
  ripple burst on activation, then continuous shimmer (flicker + subtle colour pulse).
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **D for spawning enemies (no screen space
  effects), D for players (with screen space effects).** Rationale: a brief burst on
  activation gives the 'glitch' hit, then a continuous shimmer maintains the state
  read; the agent's recommended option was D.
- **Q2 — Should enemies emerging from the wormhole receive the same screen-wide phase
  treatment or a per-enemy effect?** Options: (A) same screen-wide effect; (B) per-enemy
  personal shimmer/glow as it grows; (C) wormhole-position glow/pulse ring + standard
  screen-wide effect when phase-shift is active.
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B + wormhole effect — no screen space
  effects.** Rationale: per-entity shimmer/glow during growth plus a subtle wormhole
  ring, with no screen-wide overlays on the emergence path.
- **Q3 — Colour palette/style for the shimmer/glitch?** Options: (A) keep the existing
  cyan/red split but more vivid (higher alpha, wider offset, pulsing); (B) purple/violet
  palette (wormhole colours); (C) neutral desaturated + subtle RGB-shift (CRT).
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A.** Rationale: preserve the established
  phase-shift identity while making it clearly more visible; the agent's recommended
  option was A.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTE8EBVD0010T0Z** – Unit tests: P6 Phase Shift - pass-through, expiry, refresh (completed)
- **AH-0MU3VQ0JR009CSIN** – Respawn player in same spot (completed)
- **AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC** – Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, activates, activation, active, add (+373 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, acceptance, activates, activation, active (+350 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, activates, active, add, added (+310 more)

## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage
data.title: Spike: prove the shared campaign core runs headless (wave sequencer + upgrade choices)

# Per-enemy emergence shimmer/glitch

Per-entity shimmer/glitch for enemies growing from the wormhole (parent AC3), driven from the shared spawn-growth path (`updateSpawnAnimation`, `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`). No screen-space overlay on the emergence path — per-entity only. Additive and non-conflicting with the ship's `applyPhaseGhost` alpha.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each enemy growing from the wormhole receives a per-entity treatment over its growth window: a brief ripple burst as it starts to materialise, then a continuous shimmer (subtle scale/alpha flicker + soft colour-pulse on the entity itself).
- The shimmer is driven from the shared spawn state so `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and every combat gym behave identically — no divergent per-scene copies.
- No screen-wide effect is introduced for the emergence path; the treatment is applied to emergent enemies only, never to the player ship object (its ghost alpha `applyPhaseGhost` is unchanged).
- All magnitudes are exported tunable constants on `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` with code comments; performance-neutral (tweens/alpha only, no per-frame allocations).
- Safe no-op headless: helpers work with a stubbed scene without throwing, and an enemy with no spawn state is untouched.

## Test-first contract

The helper must satisfy the pre-written RED contract in
`src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` (`wormholeSpawn — enemy emergence shimmer`
suite, see its "predicted API" comment block): `updateEnemyShimmer(enemy, dt)`
plus the exported tunables/toggles (`ENEMY_SHIMMER_BURST_DURATION_MS` 150–250,
`ENEMY_SHIMMER_FLICKER_HZ` 2–4, `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ALPHA_MIN/MAX`,
`ENEMY_SHIMMER_SCALE_AMOUNT`, `ENEMY_SHIMMER_COLOUR_PULSE_RANGE`,
`ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_BURST`, `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_SHIMMER`). Flip each
`it.fails` back to a plain `it` when the implementation lands.

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — Edit: per-entity shimmer/glitch helpers.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.test.ts` — Edit: flip the shimmer `it.fails` cases to plain `it` (contract written by AH-0MVD2MTEI002MVIS).
data.title: Per-enemy emergence shimmer

# Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips

## Goal

Run the committed pipeline over the gathered footage to produce and validate
the actual deliverables and manifests: the ~45–60 s promo, the > 2 min
showreel, and several short highlight clips — all 960×540 WebM with the game's
SFX — accompanied by the selection and coverage manifests, and verify the
attention-grabbing pace criteria (AC1–AC4 of the parent).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can share a compelling promo package that
opens with action and showcases weapons, pickups and enemies.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Deliverables produced.** `capture-output/` contains: the compiled
  promo WebM (~45–60 s), the showreel WebM (> 2 min), and several highlight
  clips — all at 960×540 with an audio track (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback).
- **AC2 — Manifests produced.** The selection manifest (source WebM, series,
  mapped timestamps, motivating intensities) and the coverage manifest
  (feature → clip + timestamp ranges) accompany the deliverables; all three
  feature categories (weapons, pickups, enemies; boss when available) are
  listed.
- **AC3 — Pace verified.** The promo opens with action (no dead air in the
  first ~5 s) and cuts on peaks; verification measures the sampled non-black
  frame ratio and the average recorded intensity, and confirms they are at or
  above the documented reference band. The **reference band is documented**
  as part of this item (with the calibration basis).
- **AC4 — Per-clip intensities reported.** The manifest prints the per-clip
  recorded intensities so the pace claim is auditable.
- **AC5 — Validated.** Each deliverable passes the pipeline's validation step
  (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio present, correct resolution).

- **Covers parent AC1:** **AC1 — Deliverables at full game-native resolution.** The work produces, written under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree: (a) a single compiled promo WebM of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (>2 min), and (c) several short highlight clips — all WebM (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback) at the game's **full native 960×540 resolution** (the game renders natively at 960×540: `src/core/constants.ts`), each carrying the game's own SFX audio track.

## Key files

- `capture-output/` — gitignored deliverables + manifests
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — the pipeline under test at runtime
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — reference band documented here

## Implementation notes

- This is a run/verify item: the *code* is delivered by the earlier items; this
  item executes the pipeline and records the evidence (file paths, durations,
  resolution, audio verdict, non-black ratio, mean intensity).
- If footage cannot evidence a category or the pace band is not met, record the
  gap explicitly and create a follow-up item rather than weakening the ACs.

## Deliverables

- The promo, showreel and highlight clips + both manifests + a pace report
  (comment on this item).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the ffmpeg driver (C5) and the gathered footage (C6).

# Implement: wrapAware parameter pipeline

Implementation slice for the data-driven seam-awareness flag (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1). Delivers the single per-archetype parameter that every later slice reads, so enabling or disabling seam-awareness is a one-field change.

## Goal

Add `wrapAware?: boolean` to `EnemyConfig`, default it to `true`, seed `march` and `centipede` to `false`, and persist it through the CSV and enemy editor panel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EnemyConfig` declares an optional `wrapAware?: boolean` with a doc comment stating the default (`true`) and the exclusion rationale.
- Seed defaults in `configDefaults.ts` yield `true` for every archetype except `march` and `centipede`, which are explicitly `false`.
- `enemy-configs.csv` gains a `wrapAware` column (documented in the CSV header comment block) with correct per-row values; empty values resolve to `true`.
- The enemy editor panel exposes the field so it is visible and editable.
- `BaseEnemy` (and/or the shared config plumbing) exposes the resolved flag to scenes via one accessor — no duplicated parsing.
- No gameplay behaviour changes in this slice; build and the changed-scope tests are green.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The parameter is the single source of truth for wrap-awareness; no hard-coded archetype key lists anywhere outside the seed defaults.
data.title: Implement: wrapAware parameter pipeline

# Test: seam-aware aim angle

Test-first verification slice for seam-aware aimed fire (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC2 + AC5). Pins the shortest-wrapped-path aim maths before the shared aimed-fire seam changes, so the behaviour is specified by failing tests.

## Goal

Specify, in tests, that a wrap-aware enemy aims along the shortest **wrapped** path to the player while a non-aware enemy keeps the direct raw-position aim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test places a wrap-aware enemy near the left edge and the player near the right edge, and asserts the aim angle equals the wrapped-path angle (shot leaves the left edge, arrives from the right) — not the long direct angle.
- A unit test asserts that for a configuration where the direct line is already the shortest path, the wrapped angle equals the direct angle (no behaviour change mid-arena).
- A unit test asserts a non-aware enemy (`wrapAware: false`) keeps the current direct `atan2(target - position)` angle in the identical geometry.
- Tests cover both axes (horizontal seam and vertical seam) and the four-edge cases.
- The wrap maths is unit-tested independently of Phaser (pure function), matching the repo's pure-seam convention.
- All tests pass deterministically.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`
- `src/entities/Scout.ts`
- `src/entities/Scout.test.ts`
- `src/entities/enemyFire.test.ts`

# Implement: seam-aware aimed fire

Implementation slice for seam-aware aimed fire (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC2). Every archetype routed through the shared aimed-shot method — Scout, `march` and the Raider — gains shortest-wrapped-path aiming in one place.

## Goal

Compute the player delta along the shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam, gated on `wrapAware`, so shots can leave one edge and arrive from the opposite edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The wrapped-delta calculation lives once in a shared pure helper in `src/scenes/core/` (or alongside `enemyTargeting.ts`) and is imported by the aimed-fire seam — no divergent copy in any entity.
- `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` aims along the shortest wrapped path when `wrapAware` is true, preserving every existing gate (fire interval, shot probability, advance cue/tell, `shootEnabled`, alive, spawn guard).
- Aimed-fire archetypes sharing the method (`march`, `raider`) inherit the behaviour through the same seam with no per-class copy.
- An enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim — bit-identical angles for mid-arena geometry.
- Radial/spread/burst patterns are untouched (out of scope per parent constraint).
- The bullet wrap model itself is untouched; only launch direction changes.
- Build passes and the changed-scope tests (including the slice-3 tests) are green.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Scout.ts`
- `src/entities/Raider.ts`
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`

# Test: wrap-aware enemy movement

Test-first verification slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3 + AC5). Pins per-edge wrapping for wrap-aware archetypes and the unchanged bounded behaviour of the classic exclusions.

## Goal

Specify, in tests, that wrap-aware motion which would carry an enemy off-screen wraps to the opposite edge while `march` and `centipede` keep their bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests assert that crossing each of the four edges (left, right, top, bottom) relocates a wrap-aware enemy to the opposite edge, matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap model (position only — velocity preserved).
- Tests cover the shared post-motion wrap helper in isolation (pure function, no Phaser) including the exact-boundary and multi-edge-overshoot cases.
- A test asserts `march` still reverses at the arena edge and drops vertically, and that `centipede` still weaves within bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts` / centipede formation unchanged).
- A regression test asserts a non-aware archetype's position is never wrapped by the shared seam even when it leaves the arena bounds.
- At least one test covers each wrap-aware movement class (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) at the seam.
- All tests pass deterministically.

Wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position in the shared scene entity loop (game + gyms), gated on `wrapAware`, so the whole wrapped playfield is the arena for every archetype except the classic exclusions.
